history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration take measures to ensure adequate liquidity to finance operational requirements in the short term, including ensuring measures for the timely recovery of outstanding receivables, and formulate a comprehensive scenario analysis which covers short, medium and long-term plans to address the potential liquidity challenge.
history.administration_response: The Development Coordination Office, together with senior leadership, advocated tirelessly that Member States should fully fund the system and to do so early on in the year so as to avoid a liquidity crunch and provide financial stability in the short and medium term. As a result, Member States disbursed their funds in the early quarters of the year. The Development Coordination Office was able to mobilize $90 million in voluntary contributions in 2023, which is $21 million more than 2022 (the year with the largest funding gap).The increase in voluntary contributions mobilized in 2023 was partially due to the fact that seven donors significantly increased their share compared to their 2022 contribution (by more than 50 per cent). For the timely recovery of outstanding receivables during 2023, the Development Coordination Office took measures to ensure adequate liquidity for its recurring monthly expenses by reviewing the cash collection status on a weekly basis and following up with the donors of voluntary contributions on a regular basis to ensure timely cash receipts. The same applied to agency cost- share contributions. As a result of those efforts, the outstanding receivables under agency cost-share are zero, and under voluntary contributions are $4 million, which are normally collected within the first half of the subsequent year. Due to the unpredictable nature of the levy revenue and the time-lag in collection and remittance, there is a significant amount of outstanding receivables ($52 million at the end of 2023, of which $32.8 million is related to 2023 revenue that was mostly recorded in the fourth quarter of 2023). The Development Coordination Office has been in continuous contact with the respective United Nations agencies regarding the settlement of outstanding receivables. The Office also put cost cutting measures in place to manage the liquidity positions, such as freezing recruitment for vacant positions for six months or more, suspending non-urgent travel, postponing procurement of vehicles, postponing office renovations, reducing coordination fund expenditure and so on. In addition, pursuant to the request of the Economic and Social Council in its resolution 2023/31 of 26 July 2023, regarding the continual shortfall of funding to the resident coordinator system, the Secretary-General conducted transparent and inclusive, informal consultations with Member States during the fourth quarter of 2023. That included three informal plenary consultations with all the Member States followed by consultations with the regional groups. Member States expressed overwhelming support for the work of the resident coordinator system and conveyed a clear message that the funding situation is untenable. In that connection, the Secretary-General has now submitted a report on the revised estimates (relating to the programme budget for 2024) to the Fifth Committee.
history.board_assessment: Given that various short- and medium-term measures for ensuring adequate liquidity to finance operational requirements are being implemented, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: The Development Coordination Office remains fully engaged in mobilizing resources from the three funding streams – voluntary contributions, United Nations Sustainable Development Group cost sharing and the 1 per cent levy in line with General Assembly resolution 72/279 – while looking for more predictable and sustainable funding for the resident coordinator system in future. To ensure adequate liquidity to finance operational requirements, the Office has taken several measures in the short, medium, and long term. Together with senior leadership, it has been strongly advocating with representatives from donor countries to fully fund the system and to do so early in the year to avoid a liquidity crunch and provide financial stability in the short and medium term. As a result, some donors have disbursed their funds in the early quarters of the year. The Office consistently follows up with donors and Development Group entities for voluntary contributions and Development Group cost-sharing contributions to collect receivables as early as possible by the due dates. As a result, overdue receivables from pledged contributions under these two funding streams are not significant by the end of each year. For the 1 per cent levy receivables, the Office sends reminders to all Development Group entities twice a year in accordance with established procedures and follows up with individual entities, as necessary, to expedite their remittances. In addition, the Office reviews and analyses the projected cash inflows and outflows on a monthly basis and allocates funds to all units of the resident coordinator system in line with projected liquidity positions, applying some temporary cost mitigation measures, such as temporary recruitment freezes, the curtailment of travel budgets and the postponement of major procurement, including renovation of premises and the acquisition of high-cost assets. Notwithstanding the measures taken, the persistent shortfall in voluntary contributions continues and has been managed through a combination of prudent financial management and the freezing of recruitment in 2023, scaling back capacities in critical development areas, including to support for United Nations country teams’ joint analysis, planning, programming, advocacy and joint resource mobilization and leveraging development financing to accelerate the advancement of the Sustainable Development Goals. To address this and as part of long-term plans, the Secretariat presented a revised estimates report (A/78/753) for consideration by the Assembly, wherein it is proposed that funding through voluntary contributions be converted to funding from the regular budget. The report will continue to be reviewed by the Fifth Committee at the main part of the Assembly’s seventy-ninth session.

history.administration_response: The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented. The objective of the recommendation was to implement measures to ensure adequate liquidity in order to finance operational requirements. The Administration provided evidence that it continuously monitors the liquidity situation and evaluates and manages projected cashflows. Furthermore, the Development Coordination Office has remained fully engaged in mobilizing resources from all funding streams to the special purpose trust fund. The comment by the audit team significantly expanded the scope of the recommendation and tied it to issuance of the report of the Secretary-General on the financing of and governance over the resident coordinator system. The issuance of the report was not required by the recommendation and the audit team cannot change the criteria for the closure of recommendations. Therefore, the Administration respectfully request the closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the $53 million commitment authority granted to the Development Coordination Office is for 2025 only, and that it remains uncertain whether the Office will receive funding from the regular budget for 2026 onwards, the Board considers the recommendation to be under implementation.

history.sg_progress: Following the commitment authority of $53 million approved by Member States through General Assembly resolution 79/258 A, the Development Coordination Office remains actively engaged in mobilizing resources across the remaining three funding streams of the special purpose trust fund to support the system’s operational needs. To ensure sufficient liquidity and meet short-term operational requirements, the Office continuously monitors and manages projected cash flows, aligning fund distribution with available and predictable resources, particularly in the context of a rapidly evolving multilateral funding landscape. In addition, the Development Coordination Office is implementing measures to improve the timely recovery of outstanding receivables, including enhanced follow-up mechanisms and strengthened coordination with contributing entities. The Organization continues to plan for short-, medium- and long-term liquidity scenarios to support resilience and informed decision-making. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.
